mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings valuation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market health, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through reduced consumer spending expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in less than 45% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month declines in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 3% each indicate collapsing consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced corporate revenue visibility.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in less than 50% of instances when both RSAFS and HOUST decline > 3% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), rising interest rates compress equity valuations, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through higher discount rates and reduced corporate borrowing capacity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) over the past month signals robust consumer spending and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through sustained economic momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in less than 55% of instances when PAYEMS grows, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month housing starts (HOUST) decline exceeding 5% signals weakening residential construction and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced GDP contribution.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in less than 45% of instances when HOUST falls > 5% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent 3-month declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 1% each indicate broad economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced manufacturing output and consumption.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in less than 50% of instances when both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline > 1% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals impending monetary policy tightening, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through reduced real spending power and rate hike expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in less than 55% of instances during late-cycle expansions when CPIAUCSL rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.
